## Executive Summary

Dense content (disassembly, image dumps, minified sources) tokenizes far denser than the estimate, causing transcripts to reach the real context ceiling while the estimate stayed under threshold so compaction never fired. Affected runs filled the window and had turns squeezed to a handful of output tokens. Cline now records provider-reported input-token count per request and uses `max(estimate, actual)` for the trigger, scaling the compaction budget by `actual / estimate` so retention corresponds to the provider's real limit. This is a SMALL (~3-4h) HIGH-PRIORITY feature — Alexi likely has the same bug (needs verification).

Affected runs filled the window and had turns squeezed to a handful of output tokens. ## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Cline #14195 compaction trigger using actual token count — FEATURE GAP (HIGH priority, SMALL ~3-4h)

- **What**: Cline PR #14195 "core: trigger compaction on the provider's actual input-token count" fixed compaction trigger to use provider-reported input-token count instead of character-based estimate (~3 chars/token). Compaction's trigger compared a character-based estimate (~3 chars/token) against the model's input budget. Dense content (disassembly, image dumps, minified sources) tokenizes far denser than that, so a transcript could reach the real context ceiling while the estimate stayed under the threshold and compaction never fired. Affected runs then filled the window and had their turns squeezed down to a handful of output tokens. Fix: (1) Runtime now records the provider-reported input-token count for each request and threads it to the prepare-turn pipeline as `previousRequestInputTokens`, (2) Trigger uses `max(estimate, actual)`, so real usage crosses the threshold even when the estimate does not, (3) Estimate is kept as a floor so the very first oversized turn is still caught before any usage has been reported, (4) Compaction budget is scaled by `max(1, actual / estimate)` so retention target, message translation, and projection costs all correspond to the provider's real limit in consistent estimate units. Also raises default summarizer output budget from 4096 to 8192 (reasoning models can spend tight budget on thinking and return no summary text, skipping compaction entirely). Alexi likely has the same bug — character estimate compaction trigger with no actual-usage fallback. Needs codebase verification.
- **Why**: Dense content (disassembly, minified JS, image base64, binary dumps) tokenizes far denser than 3 chars/token. Alexi compaction likely uses character estimate only (`src/core/sessionManager.ts` compaction trigger, needs verification). If yes, Alexi has the same bug: compaction never fires for dense transcripts until the provider rejects with context-window-exceeded, and affected turns get squeezed to tiny output budgets. Implementation cost ~3-4h: (1) Capture `usage.input_tokens` from provider responses in `src/core/orchestrator.ts` (10 lines, AI SDK already exposes `usage` on response), (2) Store `previousRequestInputTokens` on session state (`src/core/sessionManager.ts`, 5 lines), (3) Update compaction trigger to use `max(estimate, actual)` (15 lines, same algebra as Cline PR), (4) Scale retention budget by `max(1, actual / estimate)` capped at `MAX_INPUT_UNDERESTIMATE_FACTOR` (20 lines). Total ~50 lines, ~3-4h. This is HIGH PRIORITY — compaction failures cause user-visible quality degradation (tiny output budgets, repeated context-window errors).
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14195 (Cline compaction trigger fix), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/sessionManager.ts (Alexi compaction trigger, needs verification), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/orchestrator.ts (Alexi provider response handling, needs verification)
- **Category**: core (compaction, session management, context-window handling)
- **Size**: SMALL (~3-4h). HIGH PRIORITY. Capture provider-reported input-token count, thread to compaction trigger, use `max(estimate, actual)`, scale retention budget by underestimate factor.

#### 2. Cline #14171 Windows CWD executable search disable — SECURITY GAP (MEDIUM priority, SMALL ~2h)

- **What**: Cline PR #14171 "fix: stop Windows resolving bare program names through the workspace cwd" disabled Windows CWD executable search (libuv resolves a bare program name on Windows by searching the child's working directory before PATH, gated on the spawning process having `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` defined). Cline spawns `rg`, `git`, and `powershell` with the user's workspace as cwd, so a repo shipping an `rg.exe` would get it executed at index time. Expose a one-call helper that sets Microsoft's documented opt-out (`disableCurrentDirectoryExecutableSearch()`), and call it at startup in every process that hosts Cline core: the CLI, the desktop sidecar, the VS Code extension host, and the JetBrains cline-core process. One environment variable covers every spawn site (file indexer, search, simple-git, shell executor, hooks, MCP, taskkill) and is inherited by children (cmd.exe, libuv, Bun 1.4+ honor it as well). Alexi likely has the same risk — spawns `rg`, `git` with user workspace as cwd on Windows (`src/tool/tools/grep.ts`, `src/tool/tools/bash.ts`, `src/core/git.ts` if it exists, needs verification). Feature gap: Windows security hardening (disable CWD executable search).
- **Why**: Security hardening. A malicious repo can ship a fake `rg.exe` or `git.exe` and get it executed by Alexi at file-search time or git operation time on Windows. Cline fixed this by setting `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` at startup (Microsoft documented opt-out, honored by libuv, cmd.exe, Go, Bun 1.4+). Alexi spawns `rg` (grep tool), `git` (bash commands, apply-patch tool, likely others) with user workspace as cwd, so the same risk exists. Implementation cost ~2h: (1) Add `disableCurrentDirectoryExecutableSearch()` helper in `src/utils/process.ts` (~20 lines, Windows-only, sets `process.env.NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath = '1'`), (2) Call it at startup in `src/cli/program.ts` (1 line, before any tool execution), (3) Add test planting a zero-byte `cmd.exe` in temp dir and asserting the real one still runs (~30 lines, Windows-only test with conditional skip on non-Windows). Total ~50 lines, ~2h. This is MEDIUM PRIORITY — security hardening, low likelihood (requires malicious repo + Windows + Alexi running in that repo) but high impact (arbitrary code execution).
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14171 (Cline Windows CWD executable search disable), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/grep.ts (Alexi rg spawn, needs verification), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/bash.ts (Alexi git spawn, needs verification)
- **Category**: tools (security, Windows, spawn safety)
- **Size**: SMALL (~2h). MEDIUM PRIORITY. Add `disableCurrentDirectoryExecutableSearch()` helper, call at startup, add Windows-only test.
